page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the N1 server family. It is configured with 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, featuring hyper-threading with 2 threads per core and a dedicated CPU allocation. It includes 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a 45 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the n1-standard-8 in the lower tier for raw compute tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register as weak or poor, with a Geekbench single-core score of 923.0 and a multi-core score of 3531.0. Memory bandwidth performance is mixed; while small-block cached reads are weak at 324.06 GB/sec, large-block uncached reads and writes achieve average ratings at 45.37 GB/sec and 34.65 GB/sec respectively. Text processing and decompression tasks, such as bzip3, perform poorly, though ray tracing tasks reach average performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 represents an older hardware generation with lower resource density and modest performance-per-resource metrics compared to newer architectures. It is suited for general-purpose workloads that require a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio but do not demand high-performance compute or rapid storage I/O. Appropriate workloads include moderate web serving, basic database operations, and lightweight background utility tasks where execution speed is not a critical constraint.
